articles.title: 'Paani' director Addinath M. Kothare to helm 'Gauri,' Prajakta Mali to play lead role
articles.summary: Addinath M. Kothare, who made his directorial debut with the National Award-winning film Paani, is reportedly set to direct his second feature film, Gauri.
articles.body: Addinath M. Kothare, who made his directorial debut with the National Award-winning film Paani, is reportedly set to direct his second feature film, Gauri. Produced by NH Studioz, the upcoming Marathi film will feature Prajakta Mali in the lead role.Announced on Dussehra, the women-centric film has already generated interest. Its poster features Prajakta as Gauri, while the story is said to explore how women can support one another in their pursuit of justice. The film aims to highlight the challenges and injustices women continue to face in society. Details about the plot and the remaining cast have not yet been revealed.Kothare said he aims to tell stories with honesty and sincerity. He added that Gauri will present a fresh perspective on a young woman’s struggles, relationships and pursuit of justice, while exploring a subject that has not been widely addressed in Marathi cinema.Prajakta Mali also drew a connection between the film’s announcement and the significance of Dussehra. She expressed hope that the story would inspire women to find the courage to stand up against injustice and make bold decisions. Producer Shreyans Hirawat said Gauri marks an important step in NH Studioz’s renewed focus on original Marathi film production, building on the studio’s established work in distribution, film rights and content licensing.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Inside Vadivelu’s new 100 crore home with traditional design, fruit garden, and modern features
articles.summary: Tamil comedian and actor Vadivelu, popularly known as Vaigai Puyal, has added a new property to his life away from the big screen.
articles.body: Tamil comedian and actor Vadivelu, popularly known as Vaigai Puyal, has added a new property to his life away from the big screen. The actor’s new house has drawn attention for its traditional design and modern facilities. Starting from the verandah reminiscent of old-style Tamil houses right up to the solar panel and surveillance camera, the premises offer an amalgamation of village-style and modern facilities. There is also a garden with fruit trees, a parking place, and a separate office room for the actor. Reports put the estimated value of the property at around Rs 100 crore, although the figure has not been independently confirmed.Vadivelu’s new house features traditional Tamil architectureUnlike a modern home built around glass walls and flashy designs, Vadivelu’s new house reportedly follows a traditional architectural style. According to Filmibeat, one of its key features is a thinnai, the raised seating area commonly found at the entrance of old Tamil homes. The space offers visitors a place to sit and spend time. A small statue of Lord Ganesha is also present at the property, which gives a devotional touch. The house seems to be a combination of traditional Tamil architecture while offering the comfort of a modern home. The large outdoor space also helps guests sit comfortably when they come to meet the actor.Solar panels, CCTV, and a private office among Vadivelu house amenitiesThe property is said to include a number of amenities for the convenience and safety of the occupants. Solar panels have been installed to meet the energy requirement, while the inverter works as a backup during a power cut. CCTV cameras are also included in the security system. The house also has a dedicated parking space for cars, making it easy to park vehicles. Another important amenity the house offers is an office located on the property itself.Vadivelu’s new home has a garden with fruit treesGreen spaces are another feature of the actor’s new residence. The garden reportedly includes sapodilla, banana, gooseberry, coconut and jackfruit plants. These trees give the outdoor area a natural setting and add to the traditional atmosphere of the property. With its greenery, open space and classic front verandah, this house is quite unique and stands out from the regular city houses. The estimated Rs 100 crore valuation mentioned in reports has also attracted attention, though no verified property valuation has been made public.Vadivelu returns to films with ‘Bang Bang’ and 'D56'The news about Vadivelu's house comes as the actor is working on more acting projects. After returning to film through "Naai Sekar Returns," Vadivelu performed in movies like 'Chandramukhi 2,' 'Maamannan,' and 'Maareesan.' Through his performances in 'Maamannan' and 'Maareesan,' Vadivelu introduced a new side of himself as an actor to his fans that did not revolve around the typical comedian roles he is known for. Vadivelu is involved with several new films, including 'Bang Bang' and 'D56.'DISCLAIMER: Figures presented in this article are derived from various public sources and are considered approximate unless explicitly noted. articles.title: Bappi Lahiri honored: Sangeetkar Bappi Lahiri Marg inaugurated; family and fans celebrate the late composer's legacy
articles.summary: Around five decades of memories, music and milestones came together in Juhu on Monday evening as the road leading to the late singer-composer Bappi
articles.body: Around five decades of memories, music and milestones came together in Juhu on Monday evening as the road leading to the late singer-composer Bappi Lahiri’s residence was named Sangeetkar Bappi Lahiri Marg. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the road in the presence of the Lahiri family, members of the film and music fraternity, and well-wishers, honouring a musician whose distinctive sound continues to resonate with audiences.For the family, the occasion was deeply personal. Bappi Lahiri’s wife, Chitrani Lahiri, son Bappa Lahiri and his wife Taneesha, grandsons Krrish and Shivaay, daughter Reema Lahiri Bansal, son-in-law Govind Bansal and grandson Swastik Bansal, popularly known as Rego B, were present at the ceremony.Speaking exclusively to Bombay Times, Bappa Lahiri said, “My dad was just 15 when he came to Mumbai. He would always say that Kolkata was his janmabhoomi and Maharashtra his karmabhoomi. We have lived in this house and this lane for more than four decades now, and almost all of his hits were created here. The mural I designed for this road combines a record and musical waves, depicting his musical journey.”His sister Reema echoed the family's pride and emotion at the tribute. “This is a big honour for our dad, who was a legend. We are all very emotional, but also proud and happy. My grandparents, Aparesh and Bansari Lahiri, are also blessing us today. Even now, my father's hit music can be heard everywhere, whether in Dhurandhar or Baaghi,” she said.Known for pioneering a distinctive blend of disco, pop and Indian film music, Bappi Lahiri enjoyed a career spanning decades, creating songs that became enduring favourites across generations. His flamboyant persona and signature gold accessories made him as recognisable as his music, earning him a unique place in popular culture.The ceremony saw several familiar faces from the film and music industries come together to pay tribute to the composer. Among those present were Jeetendra, Jackie Shroff, Udit Narayan, Ashoke Pandit, Ila Arun, Poonam Dhillon, Rohit Roy, Alisha Chinai, Anu Malik, Rajat Bedi, Sofie Choudhary, Lalit Pandit and Neetu Chandra.Jackie Shroff’s presence also drew attention as it came a day after a firing incident involving his son, actor Tiger Shroff.For the Lahiri family, the newly named road is more than a civic landmark. It is a tribute rooted in the neighbourhood that witnessed the making of the composer's music and the life he built in Mumbai; a lasting reminder of an artist whose melodies continue to find new listeners.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more.
